title: On the Accuracy of Approximate Leave-One-Out with Blockwise Nonsmooth Regularization in High-dimensions
abstract: arXiv:2610.27502v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Approximate leave-one-out (ALO) refers to methods that provide computationally efficient and statistically accurate approximations to leave-one-out risk estimation. These methods have recently attracted increased attention because of their connections to other important problems, including machine unlearning and data valuation. For empirical risk minimization, ALO methods often rely on a few Newton steps and therefore require smooth loss functions and regularizers. In high-dimensional problems, however, regularizers are frequently non-smooth. This has motivated the development of heuristic ALO methods for non-smooth regularization, whose empirical accuracy is often strong but whose theoretical justification remains limited.   In this paper, we study the accuracy of a heuristic ALO method for a broad class of non-differentiable penalties that promote block sparsity in the proportional high-dimensional regime.
